item.title: Closed Network Operation and the Network Separation Transition
item.description:
Where this page fits

This guide covers the use and management of open source in the financial sector. Its starting point is the closed network. Import, internal mirrors, and offline vulnerability management are prerequisites for every stage, including identification, use approval, and management, so they are explained once here, and each stage page points to this page with an “Applying in a closed network” box.

Documents produced here: an import procedure and import approval records, and a self risk assessment for a network separation exception.

item.title: Tool Setup Recipe
item.description:
This recipe is an example of setting up SBOM (Software Bill of Materials) generation and continuous vulnerability monitoring in a closed network. As a quick starting point, it reorganizes the existing cdxgen and Dependency-Track pipeline tutorial for the financial sector. The purpose is not to recommend a specific product but to show how to build the setup with open source, on-premises tools.

Closed network assumptions

The example below includes a step that downloads tool images. In a closed network, obtain the images and vulnerability databases from outside, move them to the internal container registry and mirror, and configure the tools to pull only from inside. For the import procedure, see Closed Network Operation.
